## Hiring Funnel Visualization Plan

Use the dataset to show both the **conversion path** and the **quality of sourcing**. The best view is a funnel for stage drop-off, a line chart for trend over stages, and a stacked bar chart for source performance.

## Recommended Charts and Metrics

| Chart Type | What It Should Show | Best Metrics | Why It Helps |
|---|---|---|---|
| Funnel chart | Candidate movement through hiring stages | Applications, Phone Screen, Technical Interview, Final Interview, Offers, Accepted | Makes drop-off and conversion loss easy to see |
| Line chart | Stage-to-stage volume decline across the funnel | Count by stage, plus conversion rate if desired | Highlights where the steepest falloff occurs |
| Stacked bar chart | Source quality by applications and offers | Applications and Offers by source | Compares volume vs hiring success by source |

### Funnel Chart: What to Include
- **Applications: 240**
- **Phone Screen: 96**
- **Technical Interview: 42**
- **Final Interview: 18**
- **Offers: 7**
- **Accepted: 5**

Best funnel metrics to display:
- Stage count
- Stage-to-stage conversion rate
- Drop-off count between stages
- Overall conversion from application to accepted

Key conversions from this dataset:
- Applications → Phone Screen: **40.0%**
- Phone Screen → Technical Interview: **43.8%**
- Technical Interview → Final Interview: **42.9%**
- Final Interview → Offers: **38.9%**
- Offers → Accepted: **71.4%**
- Applications → Accepted: **2.1%**

### Line Chart: What to Include
Use the line chart to show a downward progression across stages:
- X-axis: hiring stages in order
- Y-axis: candidate count
- Optional second line: stage conversion rate

Best use:
- Show the sharpest declines visually
- Compare stage volume against an ideal target line if you have hiring goals
- Track whether later-stage losses are getting better or worse over time

### Stacked Bar Chart: What to Include
Use source-level bars split into:
- **Applications**
- **Offers**

Source data:
- LinkedIn: 110 applications, 2 offers
- Referral: 40 applications, 2 offers
- Company Website: 60 applications, 1 offer
- Job Board: 30 applications, 0 offers
- Networking: 0 applications, 0 offers

Best metrics for stacked bars:
- Applications per source
- Offers per source
- Offer rate by source
- Optional: acceptance rate if acceptance by source is available later

## Source Performance Breakdown

| Source | Applications | Offers | Offer Rate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| LinkedIn | 110 | 2 | 1.8% |
| Referral | 40 | 2 | 5.0% |
| Company Website | 60 | 1 | 1.7% |
| Job Board | 30 | 0 | 0.0% |
| Networking | 0 | 0 | — |

## Hiring Manager Insights

- **The biggest bottleneck is early funnel attrition.** Only 96 of 240 applicants reached phone screen, so the first screening step is filtering out 60% of the pool.
- **Referral candidates are the strongest source by efficiency.** Referrals produced 2 offers from 40 applications, a **5.0% offer rate**, the best among active sources.
- **LinkedIn brings the most volume but not the best yield.** It generated 110 applications, yet only 2 offers, so it is useful for reach but weaker for conversion.
- **The final close is relatively strong.** Once candidates reach the offer stage, **71.4% accept**, which suggests compensation, role fit, or closing process is working reasonably well.

## Quick Actions

- Funnel chart guidance: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/business-insights-ideas/resources/funnel-chart
- Stacked bar chart guidance: https://www.tableau.com/learn/articles/bar-charts
- Hiring funnel metrics reference: https://www.bamboohr.com/resources/hr-glossary/hiring-funnel/
